title: Torta Sbrisolona
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Mantua's deliberately crumbly almond and cornmeal cake, its name literally meaning 'the crumbly one,' meant to be broken apart by hand at the table rather than neatly sliced.
longDesc: Sbrisolona's coarse, sandy texture is entirely intentional, achieved by keeping the butter cold and only barely working the dough together, and tradition dictates it should be cracked apart with a firm tap rather than cut with a knife.
ingredients: 150 g (2/3 cup) cold unsalted butter, cubed
80 g (2/3 cup) whole almonds, roughly chopped
steps: Combine the flour, cornmeal, almond flour, sugar, and salt in a bowl.
Work in the cold butter with your fingertips or a pastry cutter until the mixture resembles coarse, sandy crumbs.
Add the egg yolks, chopped almonds, and lemon zest, mixing just until everything comes together loosely - the mixture should remain crumbly and not form a smooth dough.
Crumble the mixture loosely and evenly into a buttered round baking pan, without pressing it down firmly.
Bake at 170C (340F) for 25-30 minutes until golden.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve by breaking into rustic pieces rather than slicing neatly.
chefTips: Keep the butter cold and handle the dough minimally - the deliberately crumbly, sandy texture is the entire point of this cake.
Do not press the mixture into the pan firmly; a loose, uneven crumble bakes into the correct texture.
Traditionally, this cake is cracked apart by hand or with a light tap, never sliced neatly with a knife.
commonMistakes: Overworking the dough until it becomes smooth, losing the essential crumbly texture.
Pressing the mixture too firmly into the pan, resulting in a denser cake than intended.
Trying to slice it neatly with a knife, when the tradition is to break it apart by hand.
storage: Store covered at room temperature for up to 1 week.
reheating: Not applicable; served at room temperature.
healthBenefits: Almonds provide healthy fats and vitamin E.
culturalNote: Sbrisolona is a beloved specialty of Mantua, its deliberately rustic, crumbly texture and name reflecting a proud tradition of imperfection done exactly right.
